title: Case Study: Notification System
summary: Design a system that sends Email, SMS, and Push through one interface — channels, templates, retries, and the patterns that make adding a new channel a one-class change.

blocks.markdown:
**Design a notification system**: send a message to a user through Email, SMS, or Push, honoring their channel preferences, formatting it from a template, retrying on failure, and never blocking the caller.

- It's a favorite LLD interview because the channels are structurally identical (send a message) but operationally different (SMTP vs SMS gateway vs push provider) — that gap is where **Strategy** and **Factory** earn their keep.
- The full solution layers Strategy, Factory, Observer, Template Method, and Decorator — see [behavioral-patterns-i](behavioral-patterns-i) and [creational-patterns](creational-patterns).
- Use [lld-interview-framework](lld-interview-framework) as the general approach; this topic is that framework applied end to end.

blocks.subTitle: Functional
blocks.markdown:
What the system must do:

- **Multiple channels** — Email, SMS, Push — each with its own delivery mechanism but the same "send a notification" contract.
- **User preferences** — a user can opt into or out of a channel per notification type (e.g. SMS for OTP, no SMS for marketing).
- **Templates** — the message body is built from a named template plus variables, not hand-built strings at the call site.
- **Priority** — an OTP notification jumps the queue ahead of a newsletter.
- **Retry on failure** — a transient provider error (timeout, 5xx) is retried, not dropped.
- **Extensible to new channels** — adding WhatsApp shouldn't touch existing channel code.

blocks.subTitle: Non-functional
blocks.markdown:
What the system must guarantee, not just do:

- **Asynchronous** — the caller (e.g. an order service) fires a notification and moves on; sending must never block the request path.
- **Reliability** — a failed send after retries must not vanish silently; it needs a dead-letter path someone can inspect.
- **Scalability** — volume spikes (a mass alert) shouldn't overwhelm a single sender process.

These constraints are why a notification system is a **queue-backed service**, not a function call — see the Concurrency card.

**Noun extraction**: underline the nouns in the requirements and each becomes a candidate class.

| Noun in requirements | Becomes |
|---|---|
| notification, channel, template | `Notification`, `Channel`, `Template` |
| user, preference | `User`, `Preferences` |
| queue, retry | `NotificationQueue`, `RetryPolicy` |

Verbs matter too: "sends via a channel" and "builds from a template" are behaviors that don't belong on a plain data class — they become **strategies** (`Channel`) and **builders** (`Template`).

blocks.subTitle: Channel interface & concrete channels
ChannelFactory
blocks.markdown:
The service never says `new EmailChannel()` directly — a factory maps a channel type to a concrete instance, so adding WhatsApp means one new `case`, not a hunt through the codebase.

```text
enum ChannelType:
    EMAIL
    SMS
    PUSH

class ChannelFactory:
    static method create(type: ChannelType): Channel:
        switch type:
            case EMAIL: return new EmailChannel(SmtpClient.default())
            case SMS:   return new SMSChannel(SmsGatewayClient.default())
            case PUSH:  return new PushChannel(PushProviderClient.default())
            default:    throw UnsupportedChannelException(type)
```

blocks.subTitle: Notification & Template
blocks.markdown:
A `Notification` is the request; a `Template` turns it into channel-ready content. Keeping rendering off `Notification` means the same notification can render differently per channel (SMS is plain text, Email is HTML).

```text
class Notification:
    id: String
    user: User
    type: String            // e.g. "OTP", "ORDER_SHIPPED"
    priority: Priority      // HIGH, NORMAL, LOW
    templateId: String
    variables: Map<String, String>

class Template:
    id: String
    channelFormats: Map<ChannelType, String>   // per-channel format string

    method render(channel: ChannelType, variables: Map<String, String>): RenderedContent:
        format = channelFormats[channel]
        body = interpolate(format, variables)
        return new RenderedContent(subject: variables["subject"], title: variables["title"], body: body)
```

blocks.subTitle: Preferences
blocks.markdown:
Preferences gate delivery before a channel is ever touched — a user who opted out of SMS marketing should never reach `SMSChannel.send()` for that notification type.

```text
class Preferences:
    userId: String
    enabledChannels: Map<String, Set<ChannelType>>   // notification type -> allowed channels

    method isAllowed(notificationType: String, channel: ChannelType): boolean:
        allowed = enabledChannels.get(notificationType, defaultChannels(notificationType))
        return channel in allowed

    method defaultChannels(notificationType: String): Set<ChannelType>:
        if notificationType == "OTP":
            return {SMS, PUSH}       // security notifications can't be fully opted out
        return {EMAIL}
```

blocks.subTitle: NotificationService — Template Method
blocks.markdown:
The send flow is always the same steps in the same order — that fixed skeleton with pluggable pieces is **Template Method**.

```text
class NotificationService:
    private queue: NotificationQueue
    private retryPolicy: RetryPolicy
    private observers: List<Observer> = []

    method enqueue(notification: Notification):
        queue.push(notification, notification.priority)

    // the fixed skeleton: validate -> pick channels -> render -> send -> notify
    method processSend(notification: Notification):
        prefs = Preferences.load(notification.user.id)
        channels = resolveChannels(notification, prefs)
        for channelType in channels:
            channel = ChannelFactory.create(channelType)
            content = Template.load(notification.templateId).render(channelType, notification.variables)
            result = retryPolicy.executeWithRetry(() -> channel.send(notification.user, content))
            notifyObservers(notification, channelType, result)

    method resolveChannels(notification, prefs): List<ChannelType>:
        return [EMAIL, SMS, PUSH].filter(c -> prefs.isAllowed(notification.type, c))

    method subscribe(observer: Observer):
        observers.add(observer)

    method notifyObservers(notification, channelType, result):
        for o in observers:
            o.onNotificationSent(notification, channelType, result)
```

blocks.subTitle: RetryPolicy & Observer
blocks.markdown:
Retry logic is isolated so it can change (backoff curve, max attempts) without touching send logic; `Observer` lets unrelated systems (audit log, analytics) react to a send without `NotificationService` knowing they exist.

```text
class RetryPolicy:
    maxAttempts: int = 3
    baseDelayMs: int = 200

    method executeWithRetry(sendFn: Function<DeliveryResult>): DeliveryResult:
        attempt = 0
        loop:
            result = sendFn()
            if result.isSuccess() or result.isPermanentFailure():
                return result
            attempt += 1
            if attempt >= maxAttempts:
                DeadLetterQueue.push(result)
                return result
            sleep(baseDelayMs * (2 ^ attempt))   // exponential backoff

interface Observer:
    method onNotificationSent(notification: Notification, channel: ChannelType, result: DeliveryResult)

class AuditLogObserver implements Observer:
    method onNotificationSent(notification, channel, result):
        AuditLog.record(notification.id, channel, result.status)
```

Where each pattern earns its place in this design:

| Pattern | Where it's used |
|---|---|
| Strategy + Factory | `Channel` implementations, built by `ChannelFactory` |
| Observer | Subscribers (audit, analytics) notified after a send |
| Template Method | `processSend()`'s fixed validate/render/send/notify skeleton |
| Decorator | Wrapping a channel with retry or logging behavior |

None of these are decorative — each replaces an `if/else` chain or duplicated code that would otherwise live inside `NotificationService`. See [behavioral-patterns-i](behavioral-patterns-i) and [creational-patterns](creational-patterns) for the general form of each.

blocks.subTitle: Decorator for retry & logging
blocks.markdown:
Instead of an `if shouldLog` inside every channel, a **Decorator** wraps any `Channel` with extra behavior — the channel itself stays a plain sender.

```text
class LoggingChannel implements Channel:
    private inner: Channel

    constructor(inner: Channel):
        this.inner = inner

    method send(user, content): DeliveryResult:
        log("sending to " + user.id)
        result = inner.send(user, content)
        log("result: " + result.status)
        return result

// usage: channel = new LoggingChannel(ChannelFactory.create(EMAIL))
```

blocks.subTitle: Retry & dead-letter
blocks.markdown:
**The classic bug**: a send fails, gets logged, and is never tried again — the user simply never gets their OTP, and nobody notices until they complain.

- Fix: classify failures as **transient** (timeout, 5xx — retry) vs **permanent** (bad phone number, invalid token — don't retry, fail fast).
- After `maxAttempts` transient retries, push to a **dead-letter queue** instead of dropping silently — it's inspectable and replayable, not a black hole.
- Retries need **exponential backoff**, or a provider outage turns your retry storm into a second outage.

blocks.subTitle: Queue-backed sending
blocks.markdown:
`enqueue()` and `processSend()` are deliberately separate methods — the caller only does the cheap one.

- The caller pushes a `Notification` onto a **priority queue** and returns immediately; a pool of worker threads (or consumers) pull from it and call `processSend()`.
- **Priority** (HIGH/NORMAL/LOW) lets an OTP jump ahead of a newsletter batch sitting in the same queue.
- At scale, the in-memory queue becomes a message broker (Kafka, SQS) so workers can scale horizontally and a crashed worker doesn't lose queued notifications.

How the design absorbs real follow-up requirements without a rewrite:

- **New WhatsApp channel** — add a `WhatsAppChannel implements Channel` and one `case` in `ChannelFactory`; `NotificationService` and `Preferences` need no changes.
- **Batching for digests** — add a `BatchNotificationService` that groups low-priority notifications and calls the same `Channel.send()` per batch window, reusing every existing class.
- **Trade-off**: five patterns for one problem is overkill for a system with one channel and no retries — good design fits the scale of change you actually expect, not every hypothetical.

blocks.subTitle: Adding a channel without touching existing code
blocks.markdown:
⭐ **Q: How do you add a new channel (e.g. WhatsApp) without touching existing code?**

Implement `Channel` in a new `WhatsAppChannel` class and add one case to `ChannelFactory`. `NotificationService.processSend()` only calls `Channel.send()` through the interface, so it's closed for modification but open for this extension — the open/closed principle in practice, powered by Strategy + Factory.

blocks.subTitle: Which patterns fit and why
blocks.markdown:
⭐ **Q: Which design patterns fit a notification system, and why?**

Strategy + Factory for channels, since each channel has the same contract but different wire logic and new ones appear over time. Observer so audit/analytics can react to a send without the service depending on them. Template Method because every send follows the same validate-render-send-notify steps. Decorator to layer retry or logging onto any channel without subclassing each one.

blocks.subTitle: Handling retries and failures
blocks.markdown:
**Q: How do you handle retries and failures across three different providers?**

Each `Channel.send()` returns a `DeliveryResult` classified as success, transient failure, or permanent failure — the channel decides the classification since only it knows what its provider's errors mean. `RetryPolicy` then applies one uniform exponential-backoff loop on top, and routes exhausted retries or permanent failures to a dead-letter queue instead of dropping them.

blocks.subTitle: User preferences gating channels
blocks.markdown:
**Q: How do user preferences gate which channels get used?**

`Preferences.isAllowed(notificationType, channel)` is checked in `resolveChannels()` before any `Channel` is even created — an opted-out channel is filtered out of the list, so `ChannelFactory` and the channel's `send()` are never invoked for it. Security-critical types like OTP can hardcode a non-optional default set of channels in `Preferences.defaultChannels()`.

blocks.subTitle: Scaling to millions of notifications
blocks.markdown:
**Q: How would you scale this to send millions of notifications a day?**

Replace the in-memory `NotificationQueue` with a durable message broker partitioned by priority, and run a horizontally scaled pool of stateless workers each calling `processSend()`. Per-channel rate limits (provider throttling) become a token-bucket check before `Channel.send()`, and the dead-letter queue gets its own replay worker so backlog spikes never block fresh traffic.
